account: IARI proposes using AI rainfall predictions to control irrigation gates. A forecast of rain the next day would close the gate. Otherwise, the motor could open it when soil moisture is low. The existing research-farm controller uses sensors and preset moisture thresholds. Water savings and other benefits from the proposed AI extension remain unmeasured. A cited water-saving figure comes from separate research.

ai_role.statement: The sequence diagram explicitly proposes AI rainfall prediction as an input to irrigation-gate decisions. Its effect has not been separately evaluated; existing threshold-based automation is a different component.

claim_basis: Sources: the makers' peer-reviewed study and two reports from the makers. For the benefit itself, the cited sources include no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good Innovate for Impact, 2025 final report, printed page 819, sequence diagram for the basin-irrigation system. Contributor-supplied proposed AI integration, not an independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Proposed AI rainfall-prediction integration diagram

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good Innovate for Impact, 2025 final report, printed page 819. Project-contributed diagram of proposed AI integration into basin irrigation. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 2: IoT-Based Solar-Powered Automatic Basin Irrigation System

evidence.citation: Monalisha Pramanik et al., “Performance of Sensor-based Automatic Basin Irrigation System in Wheat Crop under Semi-arid Conditions.” Journal of Agricultural Physics 22(2), 199–207 (2022). Experimental design and results. Adds measured water savings from a moisture-threshold controller; it does not establish that AI produced those savings.
evidence.title: Performance of Sensor-based Automatic Basin Irrigation System in Wheat Crop under Semi-arid Conditions
